verdict: The Hartford's GAAP profit jumped 23% on a one-off $497 million reserve-related gain, even as core earnings fell 6% on higher catastrophe losses.

segments.name: Business Insurance
segments.note: Insurance for companies — property, casualty and workers' compensation. Written premiums grew 6%.

segments.name: Employee Benefits
segments.note: Group life, disability and other benefits employers offer workers.

segments.name: Personal Insurance
segments.note: Auto and home insurance for individuals.

segments.name: Corporate & P&C Other
segments.note: Corporate items ($58M) plus P&C Other Operations ($18M), which holds runoff and legacy asbestos/environmental business.

opex.note: Commissions and other costs of signing policies, spread over the policies' lives.

follow100Note: Revenue is total revenues including net realized investment losses of $116M. Kept as profit is income from continuing operations of $1,262M; including $61M from discontinued operations (Hartford Funds, being sold), total net income was $1,323M and $1,317M was available to common stockholders.

takeaways.title: A one-off gain lifted GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Commuting an asbestos & environmental reinsurance cover produced a $497 million pre-tax gain inside prior-year reserve development of $594 million — the main reason net income rose 23%.

takeaways.title: Core earnings fell
takeaways.text: Core earnings, which strip out that gain and market swings, fell 6% to $956 million as catastrophe losses rose to $198 million and Employee Benefits claims worsened.

takeaways.title: Dividend raised
takeaways.text: The Hartford raised its quarterly dividend 12% and returned $638 million to stockholders in the quarter, including $475 million of buybacks.

oneTimers: The $497 million pre-tax gain from commuting the asbestos & environmental adverse development cover (A&E ADC) is non-core: management's core earnings of $956 million exclude it.
Hartford Funds is being sold and is reported as discontinued operations: its $61 million of after-tax income is in total net income but not in the continuing-operations profit charted here.
footerNote: Insurer accounting: revenue is mostly earned premiums plus investment income, and claims and benefits are the direct cost.
